statusText: Green. Weekend CME halt with no live Nasdaq-100 price path; Tail sits at the low-band floor and the mapped policy state is EA_ON.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Tail remains well below the block threshold. headline: Nasdaq-100: untested hawkish repricing waits behind the weekend futures halt; tail risk holds at the low-band floor into the Sunday reopen
body: This assessment is made inside the weekend CME halt, so no live NQ price path exists and no mean-reversion failure can be developing. The verified anchor remains Friday's close: NDX 29,433.43, down 0.70%, settling in the lower part of a 29,383.92-29,752.78 range, with VIX 14.43 inside a 14.13-14.84 day range. The dominant open question is policy rather than structure. Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks lifted September rate-hike odds from roughly 35% to 57-60% on CME pricing, and the 2-year yield rose about 11 basis points to 4.34%, its highest in a month. H.15 constant-maturity yields for 27 August stand at 4.20, 4.67 and 5.19 percent for 2Y, 10Y and 30Y, and Friday's move added a bear-flattening shape more consistent with policy repricing than with a growth shock. Cross-asset alignment is only partial: sharply higher short-end yields against a calm VIX and a soft crude tape, with WTI at 83.44 dollars and Brent at 88.29 dollars after a weekly decline of roughly 4 percent as the Iran confrontation was read as a sanctions and economic dispute rather than an imminent physical supply threat. Weekend Strait of Hormuz coverage stayed rhetorical, with the IRGC asserting decisive control and CENTCOM disputing it, but without a new escalation showing market transmission. Friday's index internals were rotational rather than directional: semiconductors broadly lower, with NVDA -4.57%, ARM -6.33% and INTC -2.85%, against megacap gains in AMZN +3.97%, GOOGL +1.74%, MSFT +1.68% and AAPL +1.63%. Rotation of that kind normally reduces directional conviction rather than raising the probability of a persistent no-retracement path. Under the fixed mapping Tail 5 gives EA_ON and green. Stress is held at 26 to reflect an important repricing that no live tape has yet tested, and Confidence at 73 reflects verified current levels, yields, oil, volatility, catalysts and calendar coverage, bounded by the structural absence of a price path. A narrow danger window is flagged only across the 22:00 to 23:30 UTC reopen. The shared Finviz context file was collected at 01:46 UTC, roughly 5.7 hours before this assessment, and is therefore stale under the inherited contract; its latest-session content was not relied upon, and the same internals were verified independently through primary sources.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment, spanning Friday's US cash session, the Friday settlement and the weekend halt. The series was uniformly green with Tail held at 5 and dominant mode normal throughout. Stress sat at 25-26 while Confidence decayed from 78 to 58 as the published evidence aged across the closed weekend, before recovering to 64 and then 72 on the two most recent refreshes.
outlookSummary: The next 15 projected hours fall inside the weekend CME halt, where no price path can form; Tail stays at the low-band floor of 5 while Stress drifts from 26 to 29 as the reopen approaches. From the 22:00 UTC Sunday reopen Tail is projected to lift to 12, still inside the low band, covering the first live test of near-coin-flip September rate-hike pricing, thin reopen liquidity and two-way gap risk. It then eases to 9-11 through the Asian session and into the European morning on expected volatility decay. Every post-reopen structure is stated conditionally because none of it is observable now. Monday 31 August brings month-end flows and a UK bank holiday that conditionally thins the European handover, while the data-heavy week beyond this horizon opens with ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS on 1 September and runs to Nonfarm Payrolls on 4 September. The mapped policy state stays EA_ON across all 24 projected hours.
